paragraphs.text: Whence [come] wars and whence [come] fightings among you? [come they] not hence, [even] of your pleasures that war in your members?
paragraphs.original: Πόθεν πόλεμοι καὶ πόθεν μάχαι ἐν ὑμῖν; οὐκ ἐντεῦθεν, ἐκ τῶν ἡδονῶν ὑμῶν τῶν στρατευομένων ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ὑμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: Pothen polemoi kai pothen machai en hymin; ouk enteuthen, ek tōn hēdonōn hymōn tōn strateuomenōn en tois melesin hymōn;

paragraphs.text: Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and covet, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war; ye have not, because ye ask not.
paragraphs.original: ἐπιθυμεῖτε, καὶ οὐκ ἔχετε· φονεύετε καὶ ζηλοῦτε, καὶ οὐ δύνασθε ἐπιτυχεῖν· μάχεσθε καὶ πολεμεῖτε. οὐκ ἔχετε διὰ τὸ μὴ αἰτεῖσθαι ὑμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: epithymeite, kai ouk echete· phoneuete kai zēloute, kai ou dynasthe epitychein· machesthe kai polemeite. ouk echete dia to mē aiteisthai hymas·

paragraphs.text: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may spend [it] in your pleasures.
paragraphs.original: αἰτεῖτε καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετε, διότι κακῶς αἰτεῖσθε, ἵνα ἐν ταῖς ἡδοναῖς ὑμῶν δαπανήσητε.
paragraphs.translit: aiteite kai ou lambanete, dioti kakōs aiteisthe, hina en tais hēdonais hymōn dapanēsēte.

paragraphs.text: Ye adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? Whosoever therefore would be a friend of the world maketh himself an enemy of God.
paragraphs.original: μοιχαλίδες, οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἡ φιλία τοῦ κόσμου ἔχθρα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν; ὃς ἐὰν οὖν βουληθῇ φίλος εἶναι τοῦ κόσμου, ἐχθρὸς τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσταται.
paragraphs.translit: moichalides, ouk oidate hoti hē philia tou kosmou echthra tou theou estin; hos ean oun boulēthē philos einai tou kosmou, echthros tou theou kathistatai.

paragraphs.text: Or think ye that the scripture speaketh in vain? Doth the spirit which he made to dwell in us long unto envying?
paragraphs.original: ἢ δοκεῖτε ὅτι κενῶς ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν;
paragraphs.translit: ē dokeite hoti kenōs hē graphē legei· Pros phthonon epipothei to pneuma ho katōkisen en hēmin;

paragraphs.text: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore [the scripture] saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace to the humble.
paragraphs.original: μείζονα δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν· διὸ λέγει· Ὁ θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν.
paragraphs.translit: meizona de didōsin charin· dio legei· Ho theos hyperēphanois antitassetai tapeinois de didōsin charin.

paragraphs.text: Be subject therefore unto God; but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
paragraphs.original: ὑποτάγητε οὖν τῷ θεῷ· ἀντίστητε δὲ τῷ διαβόλῳ, καὶ φεύξεται ἀφʼ ὑμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: hypotagēte oun tō theō· antistēte de tō diabolō, kai pheuxetai aphʼ hymōn·

paragraphs.text: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye doubleminded.
paragraphs.original: ἐγγίσατε τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐγγιεῖ ὑμῖν. καθαρίσατε χεῖρας, ἁμαρτωλοί, καὶ ἁγνίσατε καρδίας, δίψυχοι.
paragraphs.translit: engisate tō theō, kai engiei hymin. katharisate cheiras, hamartōloi, kai hagnisate kardias, dipsychoi.

paragraphs.text: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness.
paragraphs.original: ταλαιπωρήσατε καὶ πενθήσατε καὶ κλαύσατε· ὁ γέλως ὑμῶν εἰς πένθος μετατραπήτω καὶ ἡ χαρὰ εἰς κατήφειαν·
paragraphs.translit: talaipōrēsate kai penthēsate kai klausate· ho gelōs hymōn eis penthos metatrapētō kai hē chara eis katēpheian·

paragraphs.text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall exalt you.
paragraphs.original: ταπεινώθητε ἐνώπιον κυρίου, καὶ ὑψώσει ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: tapeinōthēte enōpion kyriou, kai hypsōsei hymas.

paragraphs.text: Speak not one against another, brethren. He that speaketh against a brother, or judgeth his brother, speaketh against the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judgest the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.
paragraphs.original: Μὴ καταλαλεῖτε ἀλλήλων, ἀδελφοί· ὁ καταλαλῶν ἀδελφοῦ ἢ κρίνων τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καταλαλεῖ νόμου καὶ κρίνει νόμον· εἰ δὲ νόμον κρίνεις, οὐκ εἶ ποιητὴς νόμου ἀλλὰ κριτής.
paragraphs.translit: Mē katalaleite allēlōn, adelphoi· ho katalalōn adelphou ē krinōn ton adelphon autou katalalei nomou kai krinei nomon· ei de nomon krineis, ouk ei poiētēs nomou alla kritēs.

paragraphs.text: One [only] is the lawgiver and judge, [even] he who is able to save and to destroy: but who art thou that judgest thy neighbor?
paragraphs.original: εἷς ἐστιν νομοθέτης καὶ κριτής, ὁ δυνάμενος σῶσαι καὶ ἀπολέσαι· σὺ δὲ τίς εἶ, ὁ κρίνων τὸν πλησίον;
paragraphs.translit: heis estin nomothetēs kai kritēs, ho dynamenos sōsai kai apolesai· sy de tis ei, ho krinōn ton plēsion;

paragraphs.text: Come now, ye that say, To-day or to-morrow we will go into this city, and spend a year there, and trade, and get gain:
paragraphs.original: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ λέγοντες· Σήμερον ἢ αὔριον πορευσόμεθα εἰς τήνδε τὴν πόλιν καὶ ποιήσομεν ἐκεῖ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ ἐμπορευσόμεθα καὶ κερδήσομεν·
paragraphs.translit: Age nyn hoi legontes· Sēmeron ē aurion poreusometha eis tēnde tēn polin kai poiēsomen ekei eniauton kai emporeusometha kai kerdēsomen·

paragraphs.text: whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. What is your life? For ye are a vapor, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες οὐκ ἐπίστασθε τὸ τῆς αὔριον ποία ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν· ἀτμὶς γάρ ἐστε ἡ πρὸς ὀλίγον φαινομένη, ἔπειτα καὶ ἀφανιζομένη·
paragraphs.translit: hoitines ouk epistasthe to tēs aurion poia hē zōē hymōn· atmis gar este hē pros oligon phainomenē, epeita kai aphanizomenē·

paragraphs.text: For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall both live, and do this or that.
paragraphs.original: ἀντὶ τοῦ λέγειν ὑμᾶς· Ἐὰν ὁ κύριος θελήσῃ, καὶ ζήσομεν καὶ ποιήσομεν τοῦτο ἢ ἐκεῖνο.
paragraphs.translit: anti tou legein hymas· Ean ho kyrios thelēsē, kai zēsomen kai poiēsomen touto ē ekeino.

paragraphs.text: But now ye glory in your vauntings: all such glorying is evil.
paragraphs.original: νῦν δὲ καυχᾶσθε ἐν ταῖς ἀλαζονείαις ὑμῶν· πᾶσα καύχησις τοιαύτη πονηρά ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: nyn de kauchasthe en tais alazoneiais hymōn· pasa kauchēsis toiautē ponēra estin.

paragraphs.text: To him therefore that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.
paragraphs.original: εἰδότι οὖν καλὸν ποιεῖν καὶ μὴ ποιοῦντι, ἁμαρτία αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: eidoti oun kalon poiein kai mē poiounti, hamartia autō estin.
